title.en: Coastlines, islands, the Sundarbans and the Northeast hills

text.en:
Meena traced India's long coastline on a map with her finger.
"It is so long," she said.

India has a coastline of about 7,500 km along the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean, with ports and fishing communities.
Islands include Andaman and Nicobar in the Bay of Bengal and Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea. The Sundarbans in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta is the largest mangrove forest, home to the Bengal tiger.
The hills of the Northeast, with heavy rain and rich forests, are home to many communities and wildlife.

prompt.en: A friend says Lakshadweep is in the Bay of Bengal. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: It is in the Arabian Sea.
Andaman is in the Bay of Bengal.

points.en: The Sundarbans is a mangrove delta.
